claims.text: A compositionally modified AlCoCrFeNi-based high-entropy alloy can exhibit a ductile–brittle–ductile transition over a narrow temperature range.
The initial AlCoCrFeNi alloy is homogeneous and single-phase.
The initial alloy can be prepared by arc melting or a similar synthesis method.
Unmodified AlCoCrFeNi normally remains uniformly ductile and shows no temper embrittlement.
The alloy should be modified with approximately 1 at.% of an added element.
Cu is an example of a temper-embrittlement-promoting dopant for this AlCoCrFeNi-based alloy.
Controlled annealing and cooling cycles can promote grain-boundary segregation in the modified alloy.
The relevant mechanical behavior should be evaluated from room temperature to above the proposed embrittlement regime.
The composition and heat treatment produce localized solute segregation at grain boundaries.
The minor dopant segregates to grain boundaries during annealing.
Dopant segregation induces a brittle phase or weakens intergranular cohesion.
The segregation-induced loss of cohesion occurs specifically in an intermediate temperature range.
At lower temperatures, segregation is not activated, preserving ductility.
At higher temperatures, the segregated solute or phase dissolves and ductility is restored.
The modified alloy will have high ductility at low temperature, a significant ductility drop and more brittle fracture at intermediate temperature, and recovered ductility at high temperature.
Conventional homogeneous AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys do not exhibit temper embrittlement.
The transition occurs only within a restricted dopant-concentration and heat-treatment window.
Conditions outside the proposed window may produce insufficient segregation and therefore no ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
The required dopant concentration and transition-temperature boundaries are not established.

Failure of the doped alloy to show a statistically significant intermediate-temperature ductility dip or increase in brittle-fracture markers relative to the control would falsify the proposed mechanism.
